stem: A 52-year-old woman skips breakfast, stands in intense heat for one hour, feels sudden lightheadedness with tunnel vision, and experiences a transient syncopal episode. Neurologic examination is unremarkable. How is this dizziness classified?

options.A: Peripheral vertigo from acute vestibular labyrinthitis
options.B: Vasovagal presyncope due to transient cerebral hypoperfusion
options.C: Central vertigo caused by posterior fossa brainstem ischemia
options.D: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo from canalithiasis
options.E: Chronic persistent disequilibrium from cerebellar degeneration

explanation: Dizziness meaning lightheaded/faint is non-vestibular (hypoglycemia, dehydration, pooling), while vertigo means a sensation of spinning.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Vasovagal presyncope due to transient cerebral hypoperfusion
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: An 18-year-old woman presents with excessive daytime sleepiness, hypnagogic hallucinations, sleep paralysis, and sudden episodes of muscle weakness precipitated by laughter. Polysomnography demonstrates sleep-onset REM periods. Which pathophysiologic mechanism underlies this disorder?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of orexinergic hypocretin neurons in lateral hypothalamus
options.B: Excessive GABAergic outflow from the ventrolateral preoptic nucleus
options.C: Hyperdopaminergic signaling within the mesolimbic reward system
options.D: Severe intracellular iron deficiency within midbrain substantia nigra
options.E: Degeneration of suprachiasmatic clock neurons driving circadian rhythm

explanation: Orexin deficiency (HLA-DQB1\*0602) removes wake-promoting drive.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Autoimmune destruction of orexinergic hypocretin neurons in lateral hypothalamus
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: Which sequence of basal ganglia synaptic connections defines the indirect pathway to suppress unwanted motor patterns?

options.A: Striatal inhibition of GPi leads to disinhibition of motor thalamus
options.B: Striatal inhibition of GPe disinhibits STN, exciting GPi to inhibit VL thalamus
options.C: Direct striatal excitation of STN leads to direct suppression of motor cortex
options.D: Direct GPi excitation of VL thalamus stimulates premotor corticospinal output
options.E: Substantia nigra compacta projections directly suppress motor cortical output

explanation: The indirect pathway acts as a brake. Putamen inhibits GPe, which releases STN, STN excites GPi, and VL is inhibited.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Striatal inhibition of GPe disinhibits STN, exciting GPi to inhibit VL thalamus

stem: A patient with insomnia is prescribed a medication that blocks orexin receptors. Which drug is this?
explanation: Suvorexant is an orexin receptor antagonist; ramelteon is a melatonin agonist; zolpidem/zaleplon bind the GABA-A benzodiazepine site.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Suvorexant
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: Following open thoracic aortic aneurysm repair, a 27-year-old man develops paraplegia, bilateral loss of pain and temperature below T9, and preserved fine touch, vibration, and proprioception. Which vascular mechanism explains these findings?

options.A: Bilateral posterior spinal artery ischemia sparing ventral horns
options.B: Expansion of a traumatic central syrinx dissecting gray matter
options.C: Direct mechanical traction injuring the lumbosacral conus
options.D: Bilateral occlusion of internal iliac artery radicular branches
options.E: Anterior spinal artery ischemia sparing posterior spinal supply

explanation: Anterior spinal artery infarct spares the dorsal columns (posterior spinal arteries), so touch and vibration remain intact.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Anterior spinal artery ischemia sparing posterior spinal supply

stem: Which inner ear receptor structure detects angular acceleration during dynamic head rotation?

options.D: Basilar organ of Corti in cochlea

explanation: The semicircular canals detect rotation through the cupula; utricle and saccule detect linear acceleration and head position.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Crista ampullaris in semicircular canals
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: What is the primary physiological function of the internal segment of the globus pallidus (GPi) in the basal ganglia circuit?

options.A: Provides continuous glutamatergic excitation to the motor thalamus
options.B: Synthesizes and delivers dopamine to striatal medium spiny neurons
options.C: Directly stimulates primary motor cortex pyramidal tract neurons
options.D: Tonically inhibits VL thalamus until disinhibited by direct pathway
options.E: Projects directly to spinal motor neurons via descending tracts

explanation: GPi normally suppresses VL until the direct pathway disinhibits it.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Tonically inhibits VL thalamus until disinhibited by direct pathway

stem: A premature infant (26 weeks, 800 g) develops abnormal vascular growth at the border of vascular and avascular retina. Which mediator drives the pathology, and what is targeted therapy?
explanation: Retinopathy of prematurity is driven by VEGF-mediated neovascularization and treated with anti-VEGF or laser.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: VEGF; anti-VEGF injection or laser

stem: A 65-year-old man presents with flashes of light, numerous new dark floaters, and a dark shadow progressing over his right visual field. What pathophysiologic mechanism directly causes outer retinal photoreceptor degeneration in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment?

options.A: Markedly elevated intraocular pressure compressing axonal transport
options.B: Vitreous humor blood leakage inducing acute photochemical toxicity
options.C: Corneal endothelial swelling blocking aqueous nutrient diffusion
options.D: Trabecular outflow obstruction depleting anterior ciliary perfusion
options.E: Separation of neurosensory retina from choroidal vascular support

explanation: In retinal detachment, the outer retina depends on the choroid for blood supply and on the RPE for photoreceptor support.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Separation of neurosensory retina from choroidal vascular support

stem: An infant has tearing, photophobia, blepharospasm and an enlarged, hazy cornea. Which is the appropriate treatment?
explanation: This is congenital glaucoma (blepharospasm, tearing, photophobia triad), a trabecular meshwork malformation treated surgically.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Goniotomy or trabeculotomy

stem: Which thalamic nucleus relays auditory information to the transverse temporal (Heschl) gyrus?
explanation: The medial geniculate nucleus sends fibers through the sublenticular internal capsule to Heschl gyrus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Medial geniculate nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: In idiopathic Bell palsy, which association and treatment apply?
explanation: Idiopathic Bell palsy is linked to HSV-1 and treated with glucocorticoids.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: HSV-1; glucocorticoids

stem: In darkness, retinal photoreceptors are depolarized and continuously release glutamate; light causes them to hyperpolarize. Which retinal neuron is the first in the visual pathway to generate action potentials?
explanation: Photoreceptors and bipolar cells use graded potentials; ganglion cells are the first neurons to fire action potentials, and their axons form the optic nerve, chiasm and tract.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ganglion cell

stem: A 57-year-old man has dysphagia, tongue atrophy, hand weakness, 1+ reflexes on the right, 4+ reflexes on the left with an extensor plantar response, and intact sensation. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: ALS combines LMN signs (tongue atrophy, hyporeflexia in the right limbs) and UMN signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski) without sensory loss. Bulbar involvement worsens prognosis.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: In Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection), which neurologic finding is characteristically identified specifically at the exact level of the cord lesion?

options.B: Bilateral loss of vibration and joint position sense
options.C: Dissociated contralateral loss of light tactile touch
options.D: Complete preservation of all somatic motor functions
options.E: Ipsilateral flaccid paralysis with focal muscle wasting

explanation: At the level of a hemisection the anterior horn is damaged, giving ipsilateral LMN weakness in that myotome.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ipsilateral flaccid paralysis with focal muscle wasting

stem: A patient with a left pontine lesion that involves the left PPRF/abducens nucleus and the left MLF can only move one eye horizontally. Which movement remains?
explanation: In one-and-a-half syndrome, only abduction of the contralateral (right) eye is preserved.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right eye abduction

stem: Which structures make up the striatum?
explanation: The striatum is the caudate plus putamen; putamen plus globus pallidus form the lentiform nucleus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Caudate and putamen

stem: A patient has a complete right oculomotor nerve lesion with an intact optic pathway. When light is shone into the LEFT eye, what is observed?

options.A: Left pupil constricts; right pupil does not
options.C: Right pupil constricts; left pupil does not

explanation: The efferent limb (right CN III) is cut, so the right pupil never constricts, but the left pupil constricts directly when light enters the left eye.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left pupil constricts; right pupil does not

stem: A 19-year-old woman has left-sided drooping of the mouth, cannot close the left eye and cannot raise the left eyebrow. Which lesion is most likely?

options.A: Left CN VII lower motor neuron

explanation: Upper face involvement indicates a facial nerve/nucleus (LMN) lesion, as in Bell palsy.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left CN VII lower motor neuron

stem: A patient suffers an ischemic stroke resulting in an isolated lesion of the left paramedian pontine reticular formation (PPRF). Which oculomotor deficit is expected on conjugate horizontal gaze examination?

options.A: Isolated left eye adduction deficit with right abducting nystagmus
options.B: Complete vertical saccadic gaze paralysis with preserved horizontal gaze
options.C: Loss of active convergence accommodation with normal lateral excursion
options.D: Inability to look right, with tonic ocular deviation toward the left
options.E: Inability to look left, with tonic ocular deviation toward the right

explanation: The PPRF drives the ipsilateral abducens nucleus (lateral rectus) and, via the MLF, the contralateral medial rectus. Loss gives an ipsilateral gaze palsy, so the eyes look away from the lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Inability to look left, with tonic ocular deviation toward the right

stem: A 45-year-old patient treated with haloperidol for chronic schizophrenia develops repetitive involuntary tongue protrusions and lip-smacking movements. What is the proposed mechanism of tardive dyskinesia?

options.A: Progressive neurotoxic depletion of striatal dopamine stores
options.B: Postsynaptic D2 receptor supersensitivity from chronic blockade
options.C: Severe loss of striatal cholinergic interneuronal modulation
options.D: Excessive central serotonin release from raphe nuclei projections
options.E: Occult lacunar infarction involving the contralateral subthalamic nucleus

explanation: Tardive dyskinesia follows chronic D2 blockade with receptor supersensitivity.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Postsynaptic D2 receptor supersensitivity from chronic blockade

stem: An 18-year-old woman presents with profound daytime somnolence, hypnagogic hallucinations, sleep paralysis, and sudden episodes of muscle weakness precipitated by laughter. Which polysomnographic finding confirms the diagnosis?

options.A: Normal sleep latency accompanied by prolonged slow-wave delta sleep
options.B: Complete absence of REM sleep epochs across overnight monitoring
options.C: Mean sleep latency under 8 minutes with multiple sleep-onset REM periods
options.D: Continuous high-voltage delta wave intrusion during wakeful testing
options.E: Fragmented N3 slow-wave sleep secondary to obstructive apneas

explanation: Narcolepsy with cataplexy: the multiple sleep latency test shows sleep latency under 8 minutes (polysomnography shows rapid REM entry). Treatment: stimulants such as modafinil, sleep hygiene and scheduled naps, with SSRIs/SNRIs to suppress REM-related symptoms.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Mean sleep latency under 8 minutes with multiple sleep-onset REM periods
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 40-year-old woman has severe low back pain radiating down both legs, saddle anesthesia, flaccid lower limb weakness and urinary retention. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Cauda equina involves lumbosacral roots: LMN signs, radicular pain and saddle anesthesia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Cauda equina syndrome

stem: A 68-year-old man with Parkinson disease experiencing end-of-dose 'wearing off' motor fluctuations is prescribed entacapone. What is its therapeutic mechanism of action?

options.A: Selective inhibition of central monoamine oxidase type B
options.B: Stimulation of presynaptic dopamine release from vesicles
options.C: Competitive inhibition of the presynaptic dopamine transporter
options.D: Irreversible inhibition of central aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase
options.E: Peripheral inhibition of COMT, prolonging levodopa half-life

explanation: COMT inhibitors (entacapone; tolcapone is hepatotoxic) extend levodopa action and reduce wearing-off.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Peripheral inhibition of COMT, prolonging levodopa half-life

stem: A man with Parkinson disease for 6 years notes that his symptoms return before the next levodopa dose. Which term describes this?
explanation: Wearing off: symptoms return despite persisting plasma drug levels as disease progresses. This leads to on-off fluctuations.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Wearing-off phenomenon

stem: A 55-year-old man repeatedly punches and kicks during sleep and has injured his bed partner, with no recollection of his nocturnal behaviors upon waking. Which sleep stage and neurodegenerative risk are associated with this condition?

options.A: N3 slow-wave sleep; future risk of recurrent somnambulism
options.B: N2 light sleep; future risk of severe nocturnal bruxism
options.C: N1 transitional sleep; future risk of benign physiologic hypnic jerks
options.D: REM sleep without atonia; future risk of Parkinson disease or DLB
options.E: N3 slow-wave sleep; future risk of intractable night terrors

explanation: REM sleep behavior disorder is loss of REM atonia and is associated with Parkinson disease and Lewy body dementia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: REM sleep without atonia; future risk of Parkinson disease or DLB
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 24-year-old man repeatedly trips over objects located on his right side. Brain MRI reveals an isolated lesion within the deep white matter of the left parietal lobe. Which visual deficit and pathway involvement best fit this presentation?

options.A: Right homonymous hemianopia – visual calcarine cortex
options.B: Right homonymous superior quadrantanopia – temporal Meyer loop
options.C: Left homonymous inferior quadrantanopia – parietal dorsal loop
options.D: Bitemporal heteronymous hemianopia – decussating optic chiasm
options.E: Right homonymous inferior quadrantanopia – parietal dorsal loop

explanation: The superior optic radiations (dorsal loop) run through the parietal lobe and serve the lower visual field ("pie on the floor"). A left parietal lesion gives a right inferior quadrantanopia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right homonymous inferior quadrantanopia – parietal dorsal loop

stem: A hospitalized patient treated for gram-negative sepsis develops tinnitus and high-frequency hearing loss. Which drug class is most likely responsible?
explanation: Aminoglycosides, cisplatin, salicylates and loop diuretics are ototoxic.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Aminoglycosides
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 60-year-old with tremor-predominant Parkinson disease is given benztropine. Which adverse effect is expected?
explanation: Anticholinergics cause dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation and blurred vision (confusion in the elderly). They help tremor but not bradykinesia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Urinary retention with dry mouth

stem: A patient presents with an isolated right lower facial weakness that spares the forehead musculature. What is the most caudal neuroanatomical level at which the causative corticobulbar lesion could be situated?
explanation: The facial nucleus lies in the caudal pons, so a corticobulbar lesion must be at or above that level.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Rostral to caudal pontine nucleus

stem: A patient presents with acute continuous vertigo and gait instability. Which physical examination feature most strongly supports a central brainstem or cerebellar etiology rather than a peripheral vestibular lesion?

options.A: Pure vertical nystagmus unsuppressed by visual fixation
options.B: Unidirectional horizontal nystagmus that fatigues with repetition
options.C: Prominent ipsilateral sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus
options.D: Severe rotational spinning with intense autonomic nausea and vomiting
options.E: Complete suppression of nystagmus when the patient fixes their gaze

explanation: Central vertigo is milder, not fatigable, nystagmus is not suppressed by fixation, there are associated brainstem/cerebellar signs and no hearing loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Pure vertical nystagmus unsuppressed by visual fixation
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which set of findings indicates a lower motor neuron lesion?

options.A: Increased tone, increased reflexes, Babinski sign
options.D: Decreased tone, decreased reflexes, fasciculations and atrophy

explanation: LMN signs: weakness, hypotonia, hyporeflexia, fasciculations, atrophy. Damage anywhere along the motor neuron (cell body, root, nerve) gives the same deficit.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Decreased tone, decreased reflexes, fasciculations and atrophy

stem: A 25-year-old man has progressive night blindness and loss of peripheral vision. His father had similar symptoms. Fundoscopy shows bone-spicule pigment in the periphery. The abnormal ERG reflects which pathology?
explanation: Retinitis pigmentosa is an inherited loss of photoreceptors (rods first), producing night blindness, tunnel vision and an abnormal ERG.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Photoreceptor degeneration

stem: A 58-year-old man dies of respiratory failure secondary to progressive amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Which neuropathologic findings are characteristically observed on postmortem examination?

options.A: Alpha-synuclein-positive cytoplasmic Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra
options.B: Intranuclear huntingtin polyglutamine aggregates in caudate projection neurons
options.C: Lipofuscin and drusen accumulation beneath the retinal pigment epithelium
options.D: Bunina bodies, TDP-43 inclusions, and anterior spinal root atrophy
options.E: Perivascular copper deposition and Alzheimer type II astrocytosis in liver

explanation: ALS pathology: gliosis, Bunina bodies, TDP-43 accumulation and ventral root atrophy.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Bunina bodies, TDP-43 inclusions, and anterior spinal root atrophy
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A 7-year-old girl sits up in bed screaming inconsolably during the first third of the night with tachycardia and diaphoresis, cannot be comforted, and has total amnesia of the event the next morning. Which diagnosis is most likely?

options.A: Sleep terror disorder occurring during non-REM slow wave sleep
options.B: Nightmare disorder occurring during vivid dream REM sleep
options.C: REM sleep behavior disorder with loss of motor muscle atonia
options.D: Pediatric narcolepsy type 1 with sudden cataplectic collapse
options.E: Isolated recurrent hypnopompic sleep paralysis episodes

explanation: Night terrors arise from deep non-REM sleep with no recall.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Sleep terror disorder occurring during non-REM slow wave sleep
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: Which statement correctly describes the regulatory actions of nigrostriatal dopamine on striatal medium spiny neurons?

options.A: D1 inhibits direct pathway neurons; D2 excites indirect pathway neurons
options.B: D1 and D2 receptors both exert inhibitory effects on striatal projection neurons
options.C: D2 excites direct pathway neurons; D1 inhibits indirect pathway neurons
options.D: D1 excites the direct pathway; D2 inhibits the indirect pathway to promote movement
options.E: Dopamine reduces net thalamocortical output by suppressing both striatal pathways

explanation: D1 receptors excite the direct pathway, D2 receptors inhibit the indirect pathway, so dopamine increases VL activity through both.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: D1 excites the direct pathway; D2 inhibits the indirect pathway to promote movement

stem: Which circuit disruption explains the violent, flinging limb movements observed in hemiballismus following a subthalamic nucleus stroke?

options.A: Massive release of dopamine into the striatum from pars compacta
options.B: Selective loss of direct pathway GABAergic striatal projection neurons
options.C: Hyperactivity of the internal segment of the globus pallidus
options.D: Infarction of ventral lateral thalamic motor nuclei
options.E: Loss of STN excitation to GPi disinhibits the motor thalamus

explanation: Loss of the subthalamic nucleus removes excitation of GPi, so the indirect brake fails and the direct pathway is unopposed.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Loss of STN excitation to GPi disinhibits the motor thalamus

stem: Why does a unilateral upper motor neuron (corticobulbar) lesion spare the forehead muscles on the affected side of the face?

options.A: Frontalis muscles receive sensory and motor innervation exclusively from CN V
options.B: Motor neurons supplying upper facial muscles receive bilateral cortical drive
options.C: Forehead muscles are innervated by the ascending branches of cervical plexus
options.D: Corticobulbar fibers decussate entirely caudal to the facial motor nucleus
options.E: Frontalis and orbicularis oculi muscles do not require lower motor innervation

explanation: Upper-face motor neurons get bilateral corticobulbar input; lower-face neurons get contralateral input only.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Motor neurons supplying upper facial muscles receive bilateral cortical drive

stem: Which genetic phenomenon explains why subsequent generations in Huntington disease families often present with earlier onset and greater clinical severity?

options.A: Progressive accumulation of environmental epigenetic histone modifications
options.B: Age-dependent penetrance restricted exclusively to patients older than 60
options.C: Uniparental disomy resulting in variable maternal imprinting expression
options.D: Expansion of CAG trinucleotide repeats during spermatogenesis
options.E: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy shifting toward higher mutant allele burden

explanation: Anticipation: more CAG repeats in later generations, producing earlier onset and greater severity.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Expansion of CAG trinucleotide repeats during spermatogenesis

stem: A patient develops spastic hemiparesis and hyperreflexia following an ischemic stroke. Which cellular mechanism best explains the appearance of hyperreflexia after upper motor neuron injury?

options.A: Heightened resting baseline discharge from intrafusal spindles
options.B: Loss of descending inhibitory control over spinal reflex arcs
options.C: Upregulation of postjunctional acetylcholine receptor fields
options.D: Selective degeneration of spinal glycinergic Renshaw interneurons
options.E: Functional denervation of Ib afferents from Golgi tendon organs

explanation: UMN lesions release lower motor neurons from inhibitory descending control, producing spasticity, hyperreflexia and Babinski sign.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Loss of descending inhibitory control over spinal reflex arcs

stem: A patient's tongue deviates to the left on protrusion with right-sided hemiparesis that spares the face. Where is the lesion?
explanation: Alternating hemiplegia: left CN XII injury (tongue to the weak left side) plus left pyramidal fibers (right hemiparesis, face spared).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left medial medulla

stem: Which anatomical feature distinguishes the primary olfactory sensory pathway from all other primary somatic and special sensory modalities?

options.A: Second-order axons reach primary cortex without a prior thalamic relay
options.B: Primary sensory afferents synapse in the ventral posteromedial thalamus
options.C: All ascending fibers completely decussate across the central optic chiasm
options.D: Primary bipolar olfactory neurons cannot regenerate from basal stem cells
options.E: Cortical projections terminate exclusively within primary postcentral gyrus

explanation: The olfactory pathway is ipsilateral and bypasses the thalamus, ending in the pyriform cortex of the temporal lobe.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Second-order axons reach primary cortex without a prior thalamic relay
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A patient sustains an iatrogenic injury to the right spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) during posterior cervical triangle lymph node biopsy. Which physical action will be most impaired?

options.A: Turning the head toward the right against manual resistance
options.B: Turning the head toward the left and elevating right shoulder
options.C: Protruding the tongue midline against opposing tongue blade
options.D: Forcefully closing the right eye against manual resistance
options.E: Retracting and closing the mandible against jaw resistance

explanation: The sternocleidomastoid turns the head to the opposite side, and the trapezius shrugs the ipsilateral shoulder.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Turning the head toward the left and elevating right shoulder

stem: Light shone into one eye normally causes constriction of both pupils. Which feature of the pathway explains the consensual response?

options.A: Optic radiations project to both occipital lobes
options.B: The lateral geniculate nucleus projects to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei
options.C: Optic nerve fibers do not cross at the chiasm
options.D: Pretectal neurons project via the posterior commissure to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei
options.E: The ciliary ganglion projects to the opposite eye

explanation: Each retina projects bilaterally to the pretectal area, which projects through the posterior commissure to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei, giving direct and consensual responses.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Pretectal neurons project via the posterior commissure to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei

stem: Which statement correctly describes the vascular and endocrine communication between the hypothalamus and the pituitary gland?

options.A: Hypothalamic arcuate neurons extend axons directly to anterior pituitary cells
options.B: Hypophysiotropic releasing hormones travel via portal venules to anterior cells
options.C: Vasopressin is synthesized and released by hormone-secreting anterior cells
options.D: Oxytocin is manufactured in arcuate neurons and released into portal vessels
options.E: Suprachiasmatic neurons secrete circadian vasopressin into systemic veins

explanation: Anterior pituitary control uses portal capillaries; the posterior pituitary releases ADH and oxytocin made in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Hypophysiotropic releasing hormones travel via portal venules to anterior cells
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: Following a motor vehicle collision, a patient sustains an occipital condyle fracture. Physical examination reveals that the tongue deviates to the right on protrusion, accompanied by right-sided tongue atrophy and fasciculations. Which diagnosis is correct?

options.A: Left supranuclear upper motor neuron stroke
options.B: Right supranuclear upper motor neuron stroke
options.C: Left peripheral hypoglossal lower motor palsy
options.D: Right peripheral hypoglossal lower motor palsy

explanation: The hypoglossal canal lies beside the occipital condyle; LMN lesions deviate the tongue toward the lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right peripheral hypoglossal lower motor palsy

stem: A 45-year-old factory worker has episodic spinning vertigo, left tinnitus and left hearing loss. Weber lateralizes to the right and Rinne is positive bilaterally. What is the hearing loss?
explanation: Weber lateralizing to the good ear with normal Rinne indicates sensorineural loss in the opposite ear (left). Presentation fits Meniere disease.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left sensorineural hearing loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: What is the rationale for edaravone in ALS?
explanation: Edaravone scavenges free radicals, countering the oxidative stress of SOD1-related pathology.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Free radical scavenging
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: An infant with weakness and failure to thrive later develops insatiable hunger and obesity. Prader-Willi syndrome is diagnosed. Which hypothalamic function is most impaired?
explanation: The ventromedial nucleus is the satiety center; its dysfunction means no stop-eating signal.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ventromedial nucleus satiety signaling
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: During tuning fork testing, why does air conduction normally exceed bone conduction (positive Rinne test) in an individual with normal hearing?

options.A: Cranial bone resonance attenuates acoustic sound propagation
options.B: Cochlear perilymph possesses higher mechanical impedance than bone
options.C: Endolymphatic fluid pressure creates negative mechanical bias
options.D: Middle ear ossicles provide acoustic impedance matching and amplification
options.E: Tympanic membrane vibrates exclusively along vertical vector axes

explanation: Sound through the external ear is amplified about 600 times, so air conduction beats bone conduction in a normal ear (positive Rinne).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Middle ear ossicles provide acoustic impedance matching and amplification
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Why is carbidopa routinely co-administered with levodopa in the management of Parkinson disease?

options.A: Crosses the blood-brain barrier to selectively inhibit striatal MAO-B enzymes
options.B: Directly stimulates postsynaptic D2 receptors on striatal projection neurons
options.C: Inhibits peripheral DOPA decarboxylase, increasing CNS levodopa bioavailability
options.D: Blocks catechol-O-methyltransferase to suppress peripheral 3-OMD formation
options.E: Competitively antagonizes D2 receptors in the vomiting chemoreceptor zone

explanation: Carbidopa does not cross the blood-brain barrier; it inhibits peripheral decarboxylation so less levodopa is needed and there is less nausea.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Inhibits peripheral DOPA decarboxylase, increasing CNS levodopa bioavailability

stem: A 53-year-old woman taking carbamazepine for trigeminal neuralgia presents with nausea, progressive confusion, headaches, and a serum sodium of 122 mEq/L. What is the pathophysiologic mechanism of this electrolyte abnormality?

options.A: Deficient oxytocin release from hypothalamic paraventricular nuclei
options.B: Impaired synthesis of vasopressin in hypothalamic supraoptic nuclei
options.C: Drug-induced SIADH with excessive renal water reabsorption
options.D: Primary adrenal insufficiency with renal sodium wasting nephropathy
options.E: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism leading to hyperkalemic acidosis

explanation: Carbamazepine can cause SIADH: excess ADH, water retention, diluted serum and hyponatremia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Drug-induced SIADH with excessive renal water reabsorption
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 34-year-old woman presents with bilateral loss of pain and temperature sensation distributed in a cape-like pattern across her shoulders and arms, with preserved light touch and vibration. Which anatomical structure is damaged?

options.B: Crossing fibers in anterior white commissure
options.D: Primary afferents entering dorsal root entry
options.E: Ventral motor neuron pools in anterior horns

explanation: Syringomyelia damages pain fibers crossing near the central canal, giving suspended, cape-like pain/temperature loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Crossing fibers in anterior white commissure

stem: A 55-year-old woman has sudden severe left eye pain with headache, nausea and halos around lights after walking into a dark movie theater. The eye is red and feels rock hard. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Pain, nausea, halos and a hard red eye after pupillary dilation in the dark point to acute angle closure. Mid-age hyperopes are at risk, and miotics open the angle.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Acute angle-closure glaucoma

stem: Which drug reduces chorea by inhibiting the vesicular monoamine transporter?
explanation: Tetrabenazine inhibits VMAT (reduces dopamine packaging and release) and is used for chorea.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Tetrabenazine

stem: A patient with a left posterior cerebral artery infarct demonstrates a right homonymous hemianopia, but central high-acuity foveal vision remains intact. Which mechanism best accounts for this macular sparing?

options.A: Foveal fibers bypass the lateral geniculate nucleus directly to the pretectum
options.B: Macular ganglion cell axons avoid decussation at the central optic chiasm
options.C: Occipital pole foveal cortex receives collateral perfusion from the MCA and PCA
options.D: Macular radiations course exclusively through the ventral temporal Meyer loop
options.E: Foveal cone photoreceptors possess intrinsic metabolic resistance to ischemia

explanation: The macula occupies a large area at the occipital pole and is supplied by both PCA and MCA branches, so it is typically spared in PCA infarcts.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Occipital pole foveal cortex receives collateral perfusion from the MCA and PCA

stem: A 32-year-old man sustains a complete transection of the right optic nerve in a motor vehicle collision. Which pupillary response pattern will be observed on direct and consensual light testing?

options.A: Right eye illumination: right pupil constricts; left eye illumination: neither pupil constricts
options.B: Right eye illumination: left pupil constricts; left eye illumination: neither pupil constricts
options.C: Right eye illumination: neither pupil constricts; left eye illumination: both pupils constrict
options.D: Right eye illumination: both pupils constrict; left eye illumination: neither pupil constricts
options.E: Right eye illumination: both pupils constrict; left eye illumination: both pupils constrict

explanation: With an afferent defect, the right eye cannot send the signal (no direct, no consensual response), while light in the left eye produces both direct and consensual responses.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right eye illumination: neither pupil constricts; left eye illumination: both pupils constrict

stem: A 52-year-old man with untreated syphilis presents with lancinating leg pains, sensory ataxia, and Argyll Robertson pupils. Which pupillary reaction pattern is characteristic of this condition?

options.A: Constricts briskly to light but fails to constrict with accommodation
options.B: Dilates symmetrically in darkness but fails to dilate under illumination
options.C: Demonstrates intact direct response but absent consensual constriction
options.D: Displays prominent ptosis with paradoxical light-induced pupil dilation
options.E: Constricts normally with accommodation but fails to constrict to light

explanation: Argyll Robertson pupil (tabes dorsalis, Treponema pallidum): light-near dissociation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Constricts normally with accommodation but fails to constrict to light

stem: A patient has a complete spinal cord transection at C2. Compared with the normal response, what is expected on testing the patellar reflex and the withdrawal reflex of the forearm to noxious stimulus below the lesion?
explanation: UMN disconnection makes the patellar reflex hyperactive, but local reflex circuits (withdrawal) persist below the lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Patellar hyperactive; withdrawal present

stem: A swimmer has severe ear pain and discharge, and the pain worsens when the pinna is pulled. Which organism is most likely?
explanation: Otitis externa (swimmer's ear) is classically Pseudomonas.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 30-year-old executive repeatedly bumps her head on upper kitchen cabinets. Visual field testing reveals a right homonymous superior quadrantanopia. Where is the lesion most likely located?
explanation: Meyer's loop (temporal lobe) carries fibers from the contralateral lower retina, which sees the upper visual field ("pie in the sky"). A left temporal lesion gives a right upper quadrantanopia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left temporal lobe Meyer loop

stem: A 3-year-old with a recent upper respiratory infection has ear pain and a bulging, erythematous tympanic membrane. Which organism is most common?
explanation: Otitis media in children: S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae, following upper respiratory infection and eustachian tube dysfunction.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Streptococcus pneumoniae
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 75-year-old man taking tamsulosin for benign prostatic hyperplasia undergoes cataract surgery. Intraoperatively, the pupil exhibits poor dilation and iris billowing. Which pharmacologic mechanism accounts for this finding?

options.A: Blockade of M3 muscarinic receptors on pupillary sphincter
options.B: Central inhibition of Edinger-Westphal parasympathetic tone
options.C: Antagonism of beta-2 adrenergic receptors in ciliary body
options.D: Degeneration of postganglionic parasympathetic ciliary axons
options.E: Blockade of alpha-1 receptors on dilator pupillae muscle

explanation: Pupil dilation uses norepinephrine at alpha-1 receptors. Alpha-1 blockade relaxes the dilator, so the constrictor dominates and the pupil stays small.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Blockade of alpha-1 receptors on dilator pupillae muscle

stem: Which of the following is a REM-sleep parasomnia?
explanation: REM parasomnias: nightmares, REM behavior disorder, sleep paralysis. Night terrors, sleepwalking and enuresis are non-REM.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Nightmare disorder
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 72-year-old woman has gradual distortion of central vision (straight lines look wavy). Fundoscopy shows drusen. She later develops sudden central vision loss with subretinal hemorrhage. Which treatment is indicated?
explanation: Dry AMD (drusen) can convert to wet AMD (neovascularization between Bruch membrane and RPE), which is treated with anti-VEGF.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Intravitreal anti-VEGF

stem: A patient with spasticity is prescribed a centrally acting alpha-2 agonist that reduces excitatory noradrenergic input to alpha motor neurons. Which drug is it, and what is a key adverse effect?
explanation: Tizanidine (alpha-2 agonist) causes hypotension, somnolence and dry mouth. Cyclobenzaprine is TCA-like, and botulinum toxin blocks presynaptic vesicle release.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Tizanidine; hypotension and somnolence
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A penetrating stab wound causes hemisection of the left spinal cord at the T8 level (Brown-Séquard syndrome). Which clinical deficits are observed below the level of the lesion?

options.A: Ipsilateral pinprick deficit and contralateral spastic paralysis
options.B: Contralateral position loss and ipsilateral temperature deficit
options.C: Ipsilateral vibration loss and contralateral pinprick deficit
options.D: Bilateral flaccid paraplegia and complete loss of all sensation
options.E: Ipsilateral temperature loss and contralateral vibration deficit

explanation: Hemisection: ipsilateral dorsal column and corticospinal loss; contralateral pain and temperature loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ipsilateral vibration loss and contralateral pinprick deficit

stem: A patient presents with right lower facial droop sparing the forehead, right spastic hemiparesis, and tongue protrusion deviating to the right without tongue atrophy. Where is the causative lesion located?

options.A: Right hypoglossal nucleus in dorsal medulla
options.B: Right peripheral hypoglossal nerve in skull base
options.C: Right facial motor nucleus in caudal pontine tegmentum
options.D: Left internal capsule corticobulbar and corticospinal fibers
options.E: Left solitary nucleus and ambiguous nucleus in medulla

explanation: Tongue deviates to the same side as body weakness in a UMN lesion because corticobulbar fibers affect the opposite hypoglossal nucleus. An LMN lesion deviates the tongue toward the lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left internal capsule corticobulbar and corticospinal fibers

stem: A 54-year-old woman reports an irresistible urge to move her legs accompanied by uncomfortable crawling sensations in the calves at night that are relieved by walking. Which clinical evaluation and pharmacotherapy are most appropriate?

options.A: Assess for sleep apnea; initiate wake-promoting modafinil therapy
options.B: Check serum ferritin for iron deficiency; prescribe dopamine agonist or gabapentin
options.C: Obtain overnight oximetry; initiate orexin receptor antagonist suvorexant
options.D: Perform nocturnal polysomnography; prescribe bedtime sodium oxybate
options.E: Order nerve conduction studies; initiate high-dose levodopa monotherapy

explanation: Restless legs syndrome: iron deficiency, neuropathy and kidney disease are causes; treat with dopamine agonists, pregabalin or gabapentin.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Check serum ferritin for iron deficiency; prescribe dopamine agonist or gabapentin
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 56-year-old man presents with shooting radicular leg pains, loss of lower extremity vibration and position sense, absent patellar reflexes, and Argyll Robertson pupils. Which structures and pathogen are responsible for this condition?

options.A: Anterior horn motor pools; poliovirus enterovirus
options.B: Central spinal canal gray matter; enterovirus Coxsackie
options.D: Dorsal roots and dorsal columns; Treponema pallidum

explanation: Tabes dorsalis from Treponema pallidum: dorsal roots and columns, reduced stretch reflexes, Argyll Robertson pupil, shooting pains.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dorsal roots and dorsal columns; Treponema pallidum

stem: A 20-year-old man with obstructive hydrocephalus cannot look upward and exhibits light-near pupillary dissociation (Parinaud syndrome). Neuroimaging reveals a pineal gland mass. Which anatomical region is compressed?
explanation: Parinaud syndrome: upward gaze paralysis with light-near dissociation from dorsal midbrain compression (pinealoma, hydrocephalus).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dorsal midbrain pretectal tectal plate

stem: A patient has episodes of a foul smell followed by lip smacking and impaired awareness. Which structure is involved?
explanation: Uncinate seizures arise near the uncus and cause unpleasant odor hallucinations.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Uncus of the temporal lobe
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: After blunt head trauma, a patient has vertical diplopia worst when walking downstairs. With the affected eye held in adduction, it cannot look down. Which muscle and nerve are involved?
explanation: The superior oblique (CN IV) depresses the adducted eye. This is tested by having the patient look medially and then down.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Superior oblique, CN IV

stem: A 68-year-old man with atrial fibrillation develops sudden right homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing. Which artery is most likely occluded?
explanation: The calcarine cortex is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery. Dual supply of the occipital pole explains the macular sparing.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left posterior cerebral artery

stem: A physician asks a patient to track a slowly moving finger. Which type of eye movement is being tested?
explanation: Smooth pursuit tracks a moving object, whereas saccades jump between stationary targets.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Smooth pursuit

stem: Which genes are most associated with familial ALS?
explanation: Most ALS is sporadic; SOD1 and C9ORF72 mutations underlie much familial disease, and TDP-43 accumulates.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: SOD1 and C9ORF72
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: In Parkinson disease, which fundamental circuit alteration accounts for the clinical manifestation of bradykinesia and akinesia?

options.A: Nigrostriatal dopamine loss reduces VL thalamic drive to the motor cortex
options.B: Increased thalamocortical excitation causes excessive muscle co-contraction
options.C: Selective loss of subthalamic glutamatergic neurons disinhibits the GPi
options.D: Widespread loss of caudate cholinergic interneurons impairs motor planning
options.E: Excessive striatal dopamine delivery drives tonic suppression of motor cortex

explanation: Without dopamine the direct pathway weakens and the indirect brake strengthens, so VL activity falls, giving hypokinesia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Nigrostriatal dopamine loss reduces VL thalamic drive to the motor cortex

stem: A patient develops an isolated lacunar infarct of the right lateral lemniscus. Which auditory examination finding is expected?

options.E: Intact hearing thresholds with impaired sound localization

explanation: Above the cochlear nuclei the pathway is bilateral, so a lemniscal lesion produces little hearing loss, but binaural localization suffers (superior olivary nucleus computes it).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Intact hearing thresholds with impaired sound localization
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A psychiatric patient taking phenelzine develops severe occipital headache, diaphoresis, and malignant hypertension after consuming aged cheese and wine. What mechanism explains this reaction?

options.A: Acute accumulation of central dopamine in striatal synapses
options.B: Impaired tyramine breakdown, causing massive norepinephrine release
options.C: Excessive synaptic serotonin causing hyperthermia and clonus
options.D: Widespread histamine release inducing peripheral vasodilation
options.E: Competitive blockade of beta-2 adrenergic receptors in vasculature

explanation: MAO inhibitors raise tyramine levels, which release norepinephrine and cause hypertensive reactions.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Impaired tyramine breakdown, causing massive norepinephrine release

stem: A 62-year-old hypertensive man has right arm weakness, right lower facial droop and inability to speak despite understanding commands. Which vessel is most likely involved?
explanation: Broca area and the precentral gyrus (arm and face) lie in the left MCA territory.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left middle cerebral artery branch

stem: What is the expected gross finding in the midbrain of this patient?
explanation: Neuromelanin-containing nigral neurons are lost, so the nigra loses its dark pigment.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Depigmentation of the substantia nigra

stem: A 35-year-old man treated with metoclopramide develops tremor, rigidity and postural instability. What is the mechanism?
explanation: Drug-induced parkinsonism comes from D2 blockers (antipsychotics, metoclopramide).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: D2 receptor blockade

stem: A 30-year-old man develops complete anosmia following an occipital impact fall during a motor vehicle collision. Which anatomical injury accounts for his permanent loss of olfaction?

options.A: Traumatic contusion of the temporal pyriform cortex
options.B: Bilateral ischemic infarction of dorsomedial thalamus
options.C: Peripheral avulsion of ophthalmic trigeminal branches
options.D: Shearing of olfactory receptor axons at cribriform plate
options.E: Herniation injury disrupting bilateral uncal cortices

explanation: Olfactory nerves pass through the cribriform plate and are sheared during head trauma.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Shearing of olfactory receptor axons at cribriform plate
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 38-year-old man presents with progressive choreiform movements, emotional lability, and severe depression. His father developed dementia and chorea in his late 30s. What genetic defect causes this disorder?

options.A: X-linked recessive CGG trinucleotide expansion in FMR1
options.B: Autosomal recessive loss-of-function mutation in ATP7B
options.C: Autosomal dominant CAG trinucleotide repeat in HTT
options.D: Maternally inherited point mutation in mitochondrial DNA
options.E: Autosomal dominant gain-of-function mutation in SOD1

explanation: Huntington disease: autosomal dominant CAG expansion in HTT on chromosome 4, with psychiatric and cognitive features.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Autosomal dominant CAG trinucleotide repeat in HTT

stem: A 20-year-old boxer receives a blow to the side of the head, resulting in left facial numbness and leftward jaw deviation upon opening the mouth. What explains the jaw deviation?

options.A: Left CN V motor lesion causing weak left pterygoids and unopposed right push
options.B: Right CN V motor lesion causing weak right pterygoids and unopposed left push
options.C: Left CN VII motor injury causing asymmetric facial expression and lip droop
options.D: Left CN XII lesion causing asymmetric genioglossus drive during protrusion
options.E: Right corticobulbar stroke disrupting supranuclear bilateral pterygoid drive

explanation: A left CN V lesion weakens left jaw muscles, and the right lateral pterygoid pulls the jaw toward the weak side.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left CN V motor lesion causing weak left pterygoids and unopposed right push

stem: A patient with bilateral lesions of the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei has polyuria and constant thirst. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Loss of ADH (supraoptic/paraventricular) causes diabetes insipidus with concentrated serum and thirst.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Diabetes insipidus
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 70-year-old hypertensive man has sudden violent flinging movements of the left arm and leg. Where is the lesion?
explanation: Hemiballismus arises from a contralateral subthalamic nucleus lesion (often infarct), so the right nucleus affects the left limbs.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right subthalamic nucleus

stem: A seizure focus in the right frontal eye field is most likely to cause which eye movement?
explanation: A seizure activates the FEF, driving the eyes away from the focus (contralateral): to the left.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Eyes deviate to the left

stem: A 19-year-old hiker returns with a rash, migratory joint aches and new facial palsy. Which is the appropriate treatment?
explanation: Lyme (Borrelia burgdorferi, tick vector) is treated with doxycycline.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Doxycycline

stem: A 73-year-old man presents with an asymmetric left-hand resting tremor, bradykinesia, and cogwheel rigidity. Degeneration of which specific neuronal population is primarily responsible for his motor symptoms?

options.A: Dopaminergic neurons in the left substantia nigra pars compacta
options.B: GABAergic medium spiny projection neurons in the right caudate
options.C: Glutamatergic neurons in the bilateral subthalamic nuclei
options.D: Dopaminergic neurons in right substantia nigra pars compacta
options.E: GABAergic Purkinje projection neurons in cerebellar vermis

explanation: Parkinson disease: loss of dopaminergic substantia nigra neurons. A right nigral lesion affects the right basal ganglia circuit and therefore left-sided movement. REM sleep behavior disorder often precedes it.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dopaminergic neurons in right substantia nigra pars compacta

stem: A 60-year-old man is diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis after developing asymmetric arm weakness, muscle wasting, fasciculations, and hyperreflexia. Which bodily functions are typically preserved until terminal stages in ALS?

options.A: Extraocular motility, somatic sensation, and bowel and bladder continence
options.B: Pharyngeal swallowing, palatal elevation, and articulate speech production
options.C: Distal upper extremity intrinsic hand grip strength and fine motor coordination
options.D: Diaphragmatic excursion, inspiratory vital capacity, and ventilatory drive
options.E: Intrinsic and extrinsic tongue protrusion force and lingual motor dexterity

explanation: Sensory systems, extraocular motility and bowel/bladder control are spared in ALS.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Extraocular motility, somatic sensation, and bowel and bladder continence
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A lesion of the right nucleus ambiguus causes which finding?
explanation: The uvula deviates away from the side of the lesion (toward the strong side), with dysphagia and loss of gag.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Uvula deviates to the left

stem: A 25-year-old man develops cortical blindness following traumatic occipital lobe injury. Testing demonstrates intact pupillary constriction to light, but absent pupillary constriction during near convergence. Which explanation accounts for this dissociation?

options.A: Light reflex requires geniculocalcarine tracts, whereas near reflex uses optic tract
options.B: Light reflex bypasses occipital cortex, whereas near reflex requires visual cortex
options.C: Light reflex requires prefrontal feedback, whereas near reflex is purely subcortical
options.D: Light reflex is mediated by sympathetics, whereas near reflex is parasympathetic
options.E: Light reflex engages superior colliculus, whereas near reflex is driven by pulvinar

explanation: The light reflex runs retina to pretectal area to Edinger-Westphal nucleus. Accommodation needs visual cortex input to the pretectal area, although voluntary convergence still works.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Light reflex bypasses occipital cortex, whereas near reflex requires visual cortex

stem: A trauma patient has early bowel and bladder dysfunction, bilateral sacral sensory loss and mixed sacral deficits after a T12–L1 injury. Which syndrome is this?
explanation: Conus medullaris: autonomic (bowel/bladder) dysfunction, sacral sensory loss and bilateral deficits.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Conus medullaris

stem: Which lesion would cause complete deafness in one ear?
explanation: The cochlear nucleus is the last point where auditory information is unilateral. Higher lesions leave hearing intact because of bilateral projections.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Ipsilateral cochlear nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 66-year-old man presents with sudden-onset pure motor weakness affecting the left lower face, left arm, and left leg, with no sensory or visual deficits. Where is the causative lesion located?

options.A: Left cerebral peduncle in ventral midbrain
options.C: Right posterior limb of the internal capsule
options.E: Right fasciculus gracilis dorsal column tract

explanation: Pure motor hemiparesis of face, arm and leg is classic for a lacunar infarct in the contralateral posterior limb of the internal capsule.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right posterior limb of the internal capsule

stem: A patient sustains an acute ischemic infarction isolated to the right medullary pyramid. Which motor deficit will be observed on physical examination?

options.A: Ipsilateral flaccid hemiparesis sparing facial musculature
options.B: Contralateral spastic hemiparesis sparing facial musculature
options.C: Bilateral spastic quadriparesis with hyperactive jaw jerk
options.D: Ipsilateral deviation of the tongue with muscular atrophy
options.E: Contralateral facial hemiparesis involving the upper forehead

explanation: The pyramid lies above the decussation, so a right medullary lesion gives left-sided UMN weakness.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Contralateral facial hemiparesis involving the upper forehead

stem: A 60-year-old man with open-angle glaucoma is started on latanoprost. Which mechanism and adverse effect are correct?

options.A: Decreases aqueous synthesis; no adverse effects

explanation: Prostaglandin analogs increase aqueous outflow (side effect: eyelash growth). Beta-blockers, alpha-agonists and diuretics reduce synthesis; cholinomimetics increase outflow but cause miosis and cyclospasm.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Increases aqueous outflow; eyelash growth

stem: A 30-year-old woman with a right-sided spinal cord injury has a stiff, flexed right arm. Which drug acts at GABA-B receptors to reduce spasticity, and what are its side effects?
explanation: Baclofen is a GABA-B agonist (side effects: drowsiness, weakness, ataxia, hypotonia).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Baclofen: drowsiness, weakness, ataxia
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A patient with normal visual acuity and intact visual fields is unable to recognize familiar everyday objects by sight, but immediately names and identifies them upon tactile palpation. Which cortical structure is most likely damaged?
explanation: Agnosia: perception is intact but the adjacent association cortex cannot interpret the sensory information.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Peristriate visual association cortex

stem: A 38-year-old man presents with progressive choreiform arm movements, executive dysfunction, and severe behavioral mood swings. His father developed similar symptoms in his 30s and died at age 45. Which neuropathologic finding is characteristic of this condition?

options.A: Alpha-synuclein-positive Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra
options.B: Eosinophilic Bunina inclusion bodies in spinal motor neurons
options.C: Hepatocellular copper accumulation with periportal cirrhosis
options.D: Neuromelanin depigmentation of the midbrain substantia nigra
options.E: Atrophy of caudate and putamen with lateral ventricle dilation

explanation: Caudate and putamen atrophy produce hydrocephalus ex vacuo.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Atrophy of caudate and putamen with lateral ventricle dilation

stem: Which neurotransmitter and receptor mediate pupillary constriction at the target muscle?
explanation: Constriction is parasympathetic: acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors on the sphincter pupillae. Dilation is norepinephrine/adrenergic.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors

stem: Which statement correctly describes the patellar reflex arc?

options.A: Group Ia afferents synapse directly on alpha motor neurons in L3–L4
options.B: A polysynaptic arc through the brainstem
options.C: Afferents ascend to the motor cortex before the efferent response

explanation: The stretch reflex is a two-neuron local circuit (Ia afferent to alpha motor neuron) and needs no brain input.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Group Ia afferents synapse directly on alpha motor neurons in L3–L4

stem: A 50-year-old man presents with progressive unilateral sensorineural hearing loss, persistent tinnitus, facial numbness, and gait imbalance. Contrast-enhanced MRI reveals a well-circumscribed cerebellopontine angle mass. Which neoplasm is most likely?

options.A: Dural-based meningioma of the foramen magnum
options.B: Schwannoma of CN VIII in cerebellopontine angle
options.C: Destructive cholesteatoma expanding in middle ear
options.E: Infiltrative glioblastoma arising in occipital lobe

explanation: Vestibular schwannoma: a Schwann cell tumor of CN VIII at the cerebellopontine angle. It may also involve CN VII and V as it enlarges.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Schwannoma of CN VIII in cerebellopontine angle
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 48-year-old woman presents with progressive bilateral leg stiffness, spastic paraparesis, hyperreflexia, and bilateral upgoing toes, with preserved upper extremity strength. Brain imaging reveals a mass compressing both medial cerebral hemispheres. What lesion explains this presentation?

options.A: Parasagittal meningioma compressing bilateral paracentral lobules
options.B: Multiple lacunar infarcts localized to bilateral internal capsules
options.C: Chronic expanding cervical syringomyelia injuring corticospinal tracts
options.D: Intramedullary conus medullaris ependymoma compressing spinal cords
options.E: Lumbosacral herniated disc compressing the descending cauda equina

explanation: Falx meningioma compressing the medial paracentral lobules gives bilateral leg UMN signs with raised intracranial pressure.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Parasagittal meningioma compressing bilateral paracentral lobules

stem: A patient has a complete right homonymous hemianopia that involves the macula (no macular sparing). Which single lesion is most likely?
explanation: A left optic tract lesion (also LGN, complete radiations) gives a right homonymous hemianopia with the macula involved. A right tract lesion would give a left hemianopia.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Left optic tract

stem: A 61-year-old man with mild Parkinson disease wants treatment that does not worsen dyskinesia. Which drug is appropriate?
explanation: Amantadine increases dopamine release, blocks NMDA receptors and reduces dyskinesia. Livedo reticularis is a side effect.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Amantadine

stem: Which neural pathway mediates the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), keeping retinal images steady during rapid head rotation?

options.A: Vestibular nuclei project via MLF to nuclei of CN III, IV, and VI
options.B: Vestibular nuclei project via VPL thalamus to primary somatosensory cortex
options.C: Lateral vestibular nuclei project via vestibulospinal tract to motor pool
options.D: Superior colliculus projects via tectospinal tract to cervical spinal cord
options.E: Frontal eye fields project via internal capsule to pontine horizontal gaze

explanation: The VOR is carried from the superior and medial vestibular nuclei through the MLF to the CN III, IV and VI nuclei.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Vestibular nuclei project via MLF to nuclei of CN III, IV, and VI

stem: A vegan with prolonged nitrous oxide use has loss of vibration sense, spasticity and hyperreflexia in the legs. Which structures are affected?

options.A: Dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts
options.B: Anterior horns and lateral corticospinal tracts

explanation: B12 deficiency (nutritional, nitrous oxide, malabsorption) damages dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts

stem: A 20-year-old man falls asleep wearing his contact lenses and wakes with a painful red eye, photophobia and a hazy white spot on the cornea. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Contact lens overuse predisposes to bacterial keratitis: painful red eye, photophobia, corneal opacity or ulcer.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Bacterial keratitis

stem: Sleep spindles and K-complexes on EEG characterize which stage?
explanation: Stage 2 shows spindles and K-complexes (bruxism can occur); stage 3 shows delta waves.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Stage N2
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 70-year-old woman presents with progressive, bilateral inability to comprehend high-pitched voices and speech in noisy environments. Which mechanism underlies presbycusis?

options.A: Fibrotic stapedial ankylosis at oval window
options.B: Impaired endolymph resorption in inner ear
options.C: Sensorineural hair cell loss at cochlear base
options.E: Inflammatory demyelination of cranial nerve VIII

explanation: Presbycusis causes high-frequency loss from preferential hair cell loss at the cochlear base.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Sensorineural hair cell loss at cochlear base
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 62-year-old smoker presents with right-sided partial ptosis, miosis, and facial anhidrosis, accompanied by persistent shoulder pain and right hand intrinsic muscle wasting. Where is the causative lesion located?

options.A: Oculomotor nucleus within the dorsal midbrain
options.C: Sympathetic trunk at apex of the right lung
options.D: Postganglionic ciliary ganglion in retrobulbar orbit
options.E: Sympathetic carotid plexus in cavernous sinus

explanation: Horner syndrome (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis). The sympathetic chain crosses the lung apex, so apical (Pancoast) tumors interrupt it.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Sympathetic trunk at apex of the right lung

stem: Which is the correct sequence of the central auditory pathway?

options.A: Cochlear nucleus, inferior colliculus, superior olivary nucleus, MGN, auditory cortex
options.B: Cochlear nucleus, superior olivary nucleus, lateral lemniscus, inferior colliculus, MGN, auditory cortex
options.C: Cochlear nucleus, MGN, lateral lemniscus, inferior colliculus, auditory cortex
options.D: Spiral ganglion, lateral lemniscus, cochlear nucleus, MGN, auditory cortex
options.E: Cochlear nucleus, lateral lemniscus, MGN, superior olivary nucleus, auditory cortex

explanation: Cochlear nucleus (ipsilateral), superior olivary nucleus (both ears, trapezoid body), lateral lemniscus, inferior colliculus, MGN, Heschl gyrus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Cochlear nucleus, superior olivary nucleus, lateral lemniscus, inferior colliculus, MGN, auditory cortex
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which of the following best describes the role of the superior colliculus in vision?

options.A: Relay of retinal input to primary visual cortex
options.D: Reflexively orienting the head and eyes toward visual stimuli

explanation: The superior colliculus mediates head and eye orienting to visual stimuli; the inferior colliculus does the same for auditory stimuli.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Reflexively orienting the head and eyes toward visual stimuli

stem: A 58-year-old man presents with sudden vertigo, dysphagia, right-sided ptosis and miosis, and loss of pain and temperature over the left trunk and extremities. Which anatomical region is infarcted?
explanation: Descending sympathetic fibers travel in the lateral brainstem next to the anterolateral system, so a lateral lesion causes ipsilateral Horner syndrome with contralateral body pain/temperature loss.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right dorsolateral medullary tegmentum

stem: A 22-year-old man presents with chronic hepatitis, a flapping wing-beating tremor, dysarthria, and Kayser-Fleischer corneal rings. Which underlying defect and management strategy are appropriate?

options.A: ATP7B mutation impairing copper excretion; penicillamine chelation
options.B: HFE mutation causing systemic iron overload; therapeutic phlebotomy
options.C: SOD1 mutation causing motor neurodegeneration; riluzole therapy
options.D: Trinucleotide repeat in HTT causing striatal atrophy; tetrabenazine
options.E: Alpha-synuclein aggregation in pars compacta; levodopa-carbidopa

explanation: Wilson disease: ATP7B mutation (chromosome 13), copper accumulation in liver and basal ganglia, treated with chelation.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: ATP7B mutation impairing copper excretion; penicillamine chelation

stem: A 55-year-old on pramipexole develops compulsive gambling and sudden sleep attacks. Which drug class is responsible?
explanation: Dopamine agonists (ropinirole, pramipexole) cause impulse control disorders, sleep attacks and hallucinations.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dopamine agonist

stem: A 28-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis presents with diplopia on left lateral gaze. Physical examination shows failure of right eye adduction with nystagmus of the abducting left eye, but bilateral convergence remains intact. What explains why convergence is preserved in this patient?

options.A: Medial rectus activation in convergence is driven by the abducens nucleus
options.B: Convergence is an involuntary brainstem reflex mediated by frontal eye fields
options.C: Cortical convergence signals access CN III nuclei directly, bypassing the MLF
options.D: Bilateral medial longitudinal fasciculi carry ascending convergence signals
options.E: Pupillary light reflex interneurons in pretectum directly drive convergence

explanation: Convergence/accommodation uses a midbrain pathway that directly activates the CN III nuclei, so it is unaffected by a pontine MLF lesion.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Cortical convergence signals access CN III nuclei directly, bypassing the MLF

stem: A 70-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension develops sudden diplopia. The right eye is deviated down and out with ptosis, and the pupil is 3 mm and reactive to light. Which is the most likely cause?
explanation: Ischemic (diabetic) CN III palsy gives a down-and-out eye with ptosis and a spared pupil. Compression (PComm aneurysm, herniation) gives mydriasis with loss of the light reflex.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Microvascular infarct of CN III

stem: What is the rationale for riluzole in ALS?

options.B: Reduces glutamate excitotoxicity through NMDA receptor antagonism
options.D: Blocks calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum

explanation: Riluzole is an NMDA antagonist that counters glutamate excitotoxicity (calcium overload).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Reduces glutamate excitotoxicity through NMDA receptor antagonism
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: A 6-month-old infant is found to have unilateral leukocoria and an absent red reflex secondary to a dense congenital cataract. Why is prompt surgical extraction and optical correction urgently required?

options.A: Unbalanced visual deprivation during the critical period causes amblyopia
options.B: Anterior chamber narrowing causes irreversible pupillary angle closure
options.C: Persistent lens capsular traction triggers widespread tractional detachment
options.D: Capsular inflammatory leakage provokes destructive chronic endophthalmitis
options.E: Asymmetric refractive focus induces irreversible optic nerve head atrophy

explanation: Visual cortical circuits develop in the first year; unilateral or bilateral deprivation causes permanent deficits.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Unbalanced visual deprivation during the critical period causes amblyopia

stem: Paralysis of which muscle explains hyperacusis in Bell palsy, and which nerve supplies it?
explanation: The stapedius (CN VII) dampens loud sound; the tensor tympani is CN V.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Stapedius, CN VII
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which nerves form the afferent and efferent limbs of the gag reflex?

options.A: CN V afferent, CN VII efferent
options.B: CN X afferent, CN IX efferent
options.C: CN IX afferent, CN X efferent
options.D: CN VII afferent, CN XII efferent
options.E: CN XI afferent, CN X efferent

explanation: Afferent: CN IX; efferent: CN X from the nucleus ambiguus.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: CN IX afferent, CN X efferent

stem: A 28-year-old man with an epidural hematoma rapidly deteriorates. Neurologic examination reveals a dilated, nonreactive right pupil and a down-and-out resting position of the right eye. Which structure is being compressed?

options.A: Right optic tract along lateral geniculate
options.B: Right oculomotor nerve by uncal herniation
options.C: Right abducens nerve along petrous clivus
options.D: Right trochlear nucleus in dorsal midbrain
options.E: Right ciliary ganglion inside orbital apex

explanation: Uncal herniation compresses CN III, producing a blown pupil first and then the down-and-out eye.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right oculomotor nerve by uncal herniation

stem: Which brainstem nucleus and thalamic nucleus relay taste information?
explanation: Taste (CN VII, IX, X) goes to the solitary nucleus, then VPM, then postcentral gyrus and insula.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Solitary nucleus; VPM
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 52-year-old man has chills, shivering and a fever of 103°F on a warm day. He also has bitemporal hemianopia. Which hypothalamic structure is lesioned?
explanation: The anterior nucleus drives cooling. Its lesion leaves the posterior (heat-generating) nucleus unopposed: fever and shivering. The bitemporal hemianopia suggests a lesion compressing the adjacent chiasm.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Anterior nucleus
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Hypothalamus, Smell & Taste

stem: A 50-year-old man is brought in by a friend who says he has had several car accidents in recent months, mostly while changing lanes. Visual field testing shows loss of both temporal fields. Which fibers are most likely compromised?

options.A: Temporal retinal fibers of both eyes
options.B: Nasal retinal fibers of the right eye only
options.C: Nasal retinal fibers that decussate at the optic chiasm
options.D: Optic radiation fibers in the parietal lobe
options.E: Geniculocalcarine fibers in the temporal lobe

explanation: Bitemporal hemianopia (e.g., pituitary adenoma) results from damage to nasal retinal fibers (which carry temporal visual field) as they cross in the chiasm. The chiasm is the first site where a lesion affects both eyes.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Nasal retinal fibers that decussate at the optic chiasm

stem: A patient has a diminished biceps reflex and weak elbow flexion. Which spinal roots are involved?
explanation: Biceps C5–C6 (triceps C6–C8).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: C5–C6

stem: Which specific basal ganglia circuit alteration is responsible for choreiform hyperkinesias in the early stages of Huntington disease?

options.A: Degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra pars compacta
options.B: Loss of indirect pathway striatal GABAergic neurons disinhibits movement
options.C: Selective destruction of direct pathway striatal projections to the GPi
options.D: Marked hyperactivation of the internal segment of the globus pallidus
options.E: Excessive baseline dopamine synthesis by ventral tegmental area neurons

explanation: Loss of indirect-pathway putamen neurons reduces the brake, so VL activity increases and choreiform movements occur.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Loss of indirect pathway striatal GABAergic neurons disinhibits movement

stem: A 35-year-old man has brief spinning vertigo on turning in bed, lasting under a minute, with no hearing loss. Which test is diagnostic?
explanation: BPPV is diagnosed by Dix-Hallpike (positive nystagmus with provocation).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dix-Hallpike maneuver
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which protein aggregates form the Lewy bodies of Parkinson disease?
explanation: Alpha-synuclein (Lewy bodies). Huntingtin, TDP-43 and SOD1 belong to HD and ALS.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Alpha-synuclein

stem: A 30-year-old woman has progressive hearing loss with a normal tympanic membrane. Weber lateralizes to the right ear, and Rinne is negative on the right. What is the finding?
explanation: Conductive loss: Weber lateralizes to the affected ear and Rinne is negative (bone greater than air) on that side.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right conductive hearing loss
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which drug reduces spasticity by blocking calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and what is its notable toxicity?
explanation: Dantrolene acts peripherally on muscle; it can cause hepatotoxicity.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Dantrolene; hepatotoxicity
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

stem: Deep brain stimulation for advanced Parkinson disease most commonly targets which structure?
explanation: DBS inhibits the STN; pallidotomy lesions GPi to reduce VL inhibition.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Subthalamic nucleus

stem: A 28-year-old woman recovering from influenza has continuous spinning vertigo for several days, vomiting, imbalance and right hearing loss. MRI is normal. What is the diagnosis?
explanation: Labyrinthitis: continuous vertigo lasting days after viral illness, with hearing loss; self-limited.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Labyrinthitis
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 45-year-old woman experiences episodic bouts of severe rotational vertigo lasting 3 hours, associated with unilateral low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, roaring tinnitus, and aural fullness. What is the underlying pathophysiology?

options.A: Endolymphatic hydrops distending the cochlear duct
options.B: Dislodged canalith debris in posterior semicircular canal
options.C: Perilymph fistulous leakage through round window membrane
options.D: Autoimmune inflammatory demyelination of cranial nerve VIII
options.E: Thromboembolic ischemia of internal labyrinthine artery

explanation: Meniere disease: excess endolymph. Treatment: sodium restriction, diuretics, steroids.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Endolymphatic hydrops distending the cochlear duct
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 47-year-old man with a recent dental abscess has fever, a swollen closed left eyelid, proptosis, absent left corneal reflex and limited eye movement in all directions. Which set of nerves passes through the affected venous sinus?

options.A: CN III, IV, V1, V2, VI

explanation: Cavernous sinus thrombosis: the sinus contains CN III, IV, V1, V2 and VI (plus the ICA). The valveless ophthalmic veins let infections spread here.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: CN III, IV, V1, V2, VI

stem: A patient with severe fat malabsorption reports difficulty driving at night. Which mechanism best explains the symptom?

options.B: Loss of cone opsins in the fovea
options.E: Damage to the lateral geniculate nucleus

explanation: Vitamin A is needed to synthesize rhodopsin and cone opsins. Rods (dim light, peripheral retina) fail first, causing night blindness.
