high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Impaired rhodopsin synthesis in rods

stem: A college student cannot read the board from the back of the room. His eye is too long, and distant images focus in front of the retina. Which condition is this?
explanation: Myopia: eye too long, image focuses in front of the retina. Hyperopia: eye too short. Presbyopia: lens stiffens with age. Astigmatism: corneal curvature.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Myopia

stem: In the classical basal ganglia motor circuit, which sequence of synaptic interactions characterizes the direct pathway to facilitate voluntary movement?

options.A: Striatal excitation of GPi leads to heightened tonic inhibition of VL thalamus
options.B: Striatal excitation of GPe leads to disinhibition of subthalamic glutamatergic drive
options.C: Subthalamic excitation of GPi leads to increased inhibitory clamp on motor cortex
options.D: Motor cortex inhibition of striatum leads to suppression of thalamocortical drive
options.E: Striatal inhibition of GPi disinhibits VL thalamus, exciting the motor cortex

explanation: Direct pathway: inhibit the inhibitor. Cortex excites putamen, putamen inhibits GPi, VL is disinhibited and excites the cortex.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Striatal inhibition of GPi disinhibits VL thalamus, exciting the motor cortex

stem: A patient's right eye rests deviated medially and cannot abduct. Which is the most likely lesion?

options.E: Right ophthalmic division of CN V

explanation: CN VI supplies the lateral rectus. A lesion leaves the eye positioned medially.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right abducens nerve

stem: Which statement correctly describes the reciprocal neurochemical interactions governing sleep-wake transitions in the brainstem and hypothalamus?

options.A: Ascending reticular activating system promotes sleep induction via GABA
options.B: Hypothalamic orexin neurons promote sleep induction by exciting VLPO neurons
options.C: Pineal melatonin directly stimulates cortical pyramidal neurons to promote wakefulness
options.D: Ventrolateral preoptic nucleus neurons release glutamate to excite thalamocortical networks
options.E: VLPO releases GABA to suppress arousal centers, while orexin neurons promote wakefulness

explanation: The RAS promotes wakefulness; the VLPO sleep-promoting GABA neurons inhibit the RAS; orexin neurons inhibit the VLPO to promote arousal.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: VLPO releases GABA to suppress arousal centers, while orexin neurons promote wakefulness
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Sleep & Sleep Disorders

stem: A 28-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis has double vision on left gaze. On looking left, the left eye abducts, but the right eye stays at midline. Which structure is lesioned?
explanation: This is an internuclear ophthalmoplegia. The right MLF lesion prevents signals from the left abducens/PPRF reaching the right CN III nucleus, so the right eye cannot adduct on left gaze.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right MLF

stem: A 40-year-old woman presents with severe neck pain, right partial ptosis, and miosis following an internal carotid artery dissection. Which neurons are injured in this clinical scenario?

options.A: First-order hypothalamospinal sympathetic axons in lateral brainstem
options.B: Second-order preganglionic sympathetic neurons in spinal ciliospinal center
options.C: Second-order sympathetic chain ganglia fibers ascending at thoracic apex
options.D: Third-order postganglionic sympathetic fibers ascending on carotid artery
options.E: Preganglionic parasympathetic visceral motor neurons in Edinger-Westphal

explanation: Third-order sympathetic neurons arise from the superior cervical ganglion and follow the internal carotid artery to the dilator pupillae.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Third-order postganglionic sympathetic fibers ascending on carotid artery

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with brief episodes of spinning vertigo lasting 30 seconds when rolling over in bed, with no associated hearing loss or tinnitus. Dix-Hallpike testing triggers upbeat, torsional nystagmus. Which intervention is indicated, and what is its therapeutic mechanism?

options.A: Stereotactic radiosurgery to ablate vestibular nerve fibers
options.B: Sodium restriction and thiazide diuretics to reduce inner ear hydrops
options.C: High-dose intravenous corticosteroids to suppress vestibular neuritis
options.D: Oral broad-spectrum antibiotics to clear infectious labyrinthitis
options.E: Canalith repositioning maneuver to return otoconia to the utricle

explanation: The Epley maneuver moves dislodged otoconia out of the semicircular canal into the vestibule.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Canalith repositioning maneuver to return otoconia to the utricle
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: Which tract maintains antigravity muscle tone for balance?
explanation: The lateral vestibulospinal tract (from the lateral vestibular nucleus) maintains antigravity tone; the medial tract controls the neck.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Lateral vestibulospinal tract
source: USMLE Step 1 Set 3: Auditory & Vestibular System

stem: A 40-year-old man with low back pain has an absent right Achilles reflex and weak plantarflexion. Which roots mediate the Achilles reflex?
explanation: Achilles S1–S2. Others: patellar L3–L4, cremasteric L1–L2, anal wink S3–S4.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: S1–S2

stem: A 62-year-old woman reports one year of painless, progressive loss of central vision restricted to the right eye. Visual acuity and fields in the left eye are completely normal. Which anatomical location is most consistent with this deficit?

options.D: Right optic nerve anterior to chiasm

explanation: A monocular deficit localizes anterior to the chiasm: the retina or optic nerve on that side.
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Right optic nerve anterior to chiasm

stem: A 70-year-old woman has an acute left MCA infarct involving the frontal eye field. Where are her eyes directed?

options.A: Both eyes deviated to the left
options.B: Both eyes deviated to the right
options.C: Left eye deviated down and out

explanation: Stroke at the frontal eye field leaves the intact contralateral FEF unopposed, so the eyes look toward the lesion (left).
high_yield_pearl: High-Yield Rule: Both eyes deviated to the left
